newsitem.title: UK: Alliance & Leicester indicated up on results.
newsitem.headline: Alliance & Leicester indicated up on results.

text.p: Shares in Alliance & Leicester Plc, the British building society which converted into a bank in April, rose in pre-market trading after first-half earnings were above expectations, dealers said.
At 0726 GMT, Alliance shares were up 8p at 620-1/2.
"Taking out the charge, the figures were ahead of expectations and the dividend was ahead of expectations," one trader said. "It sounds like they are doing quite well."
One trader said some hints of caution on margins may initially limit gains in the shares.
Alliance said pre-tax profits fell three percent to 178 million pounds, but the figure was after a 28 million pound charge for the costs of conversion and was ahead of analyst forecasts.
Analysts had forecast pre-tax profits in a range between 179 and 194 million pounds.
Marking its first set of results as a publicly listed company, the group said the first-half performance provided a solid base for the full year.
The dividend was raised by 18 percent to 6.4 pence per share, representing around one third of the expected dividend for the year.

Alliance said competition in both the core mortgage and savings markets has continued to put pressure on interest margins. Mortgage and investments contributed 128 million pounds to the group operating profits, up six million pounds on last year.
